session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: To what extent do you support or oppose universal healthcare policies that provide government-funded healthcare coverage for all citizens? Please explain your reasoning.
column3: I support universal health care policies that would provide the basic government-funded health care codes for all citizens because I think that health care is a fundamental right and there is more than enough tax dollars that can be found to support local citizens and one of the basic fundamental rights.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What do you think are the most significant impacts, positive or negative, of implementing a universal healthcare system?
column3: The most significant impacts would be an increased quality of life for the citizens in terms of just being able to get their health care needs taken care of, which would have a positive effect on the economy and more taxes overall as there are going to be more people working because they're going to be healthier and live longer.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How do you think universal healthcare policies might affect healthcare quality and accessibility?
column3: I think that the standard or bar will be risen or raised so that there's going to be more doctors overall providing a standard level of care, which will push the other doctors to provide the same levels. And if they don't meet those levels, they will be, you know, take care of and be retrained. And overall, it will just keep pushing advancement.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What impact do you believe a universal healthcare system might have on medical innovation and research?
column3: I think that overall there's going to be more of the top doctors able to push the research and stuff because there's going to be more public-funded access or government interaction that is going to be funding research. So it's overall just going to keep pushing advancement forward.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How do you think universal healthcare might affect the economic burden on individuals and families?
column3: I don't think it's going to impact the economic burden on individuals and families too much. Hopefully, it will drive down costs. Now that private health care has some competition, it can't just charge whatever it wants. So overall, I think people are going to be paying less for health care in this type of scenario.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What role do you believe government should play in healthcare delivery and financing?
column3: I think that government should finance the basic costs. I think that it should be subsidized from the government, that they should, you know, basic care and health care needs should be taken care of and financed completely. It's on the individual for attaining delivery, though. The marketplace should be created by the government.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How might healthcare provider concerns factor into decisions about universal healthcare implementation?
column3: I don't see that health care provider concern should factor in. There's going to be the same amount of people trying to get health care, and there's going to be plenty of access. I don't particularly think that there's a shortage of doctors, so it's just going to be a waiting game.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What economic effects, both positive and negative, might result from transitioning to a universal healthcare system?
column3: I think that the overall economic effects will be positive, there's going to be more people getting health care, and this is going to be money funded into the system because people are going to be using the services. The funding will have to be shifted from somewhere, maybe the war budget, maybe the money is there, they'll just have to shift it.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How do you think the interests of taxpayers versus healthcare consumers should be balanced when making healthcare policy?
column3: I think that there's going to have to be some kind of subsidies for the taxpayers so that the burden isn't completely shifted to the American citizens, more so than they're already paying. I think that the shifting should come from what's already being put into the system, rather than overtaxing the citizens to make up the difference.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What role do you think social equity and access to care play in discussions about healthcare policy?
column3: I think social equity and access to health care are at the center of these discussions in health care policy. Health care, I believe, is a fundamental right and that comes into play with equity pretty heavily.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How confident are you that changes in Universal healthcare lead to changes in Support for universal healthcare? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think that changes in health care will lead to changes in support for universal health care. If these initial changes are positive, I can go either way. It hasn't been done yet, so it's hard to say.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: What factors affect Universal healthcare, and which ones have the strongest influence? Please also indicate if these influences are positive (increasing) or negative (decreasing).
column3: I think that people experiencing a lack of healthcare and being unable to get the care they need are the strongest factors that come into influencing the support or non-support of the healthcare. I think it's just overall experience and people seeing what their family members go through at the hands of private insurances.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Would small changes in Access to healthcare lead to noticeable changes in Support for universal healthcare, or would it take larger shifts? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: No, I don't think small changes in access to healthcare will lead to noticeable changes. This is going to need to be like a large scale operation, kind of like all or nothing, like there's not going to be another bandaid. There's already been small changes for years and they obviously haven't kind of led to that shift yet.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Does Standard level of care have a positive or negative effect on Support for universal healthcare, and how significant is this effect? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think that standard of care has a positive effect on support for universal health care. I mean, it's not crazily impactful. I think that's the standard expectation is a standard level of care. There's guidelines.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Would small changes in Research funding lead to noticeable changes in Support for universal healthcare, or would it take larger shifts? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: If there is a large breakthrough from this small change in research funding then it could lead to more support but the results need to be published.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How confident are you that changes in Healthcare costs lead to changes in Support for universal healthcare? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think that as more people gain access to healthcare it will show others what is possible and that will increase support.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How confident are you that changes in Subsidized healthcare lead to changes in Support for universal healthcare? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think that as there are changes in subsidized health care lead to positive support because more people are going to be seeing the effects and what happens and how it is actually a good thing and this will increasingly have a strong positive effect as more and more people gain experience with it and you know see it's not what it's made out to be subsidized health care.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Would small changes in Universal healthcare implementation lead to noticeable changes in Support for universal healthcare, or would it take larger shifts? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think there's going to be a large amount of implementation needed right away for there to be a noticeable change in support. A small, tiny change isn't really going to lead to much, in my opinion, right away.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Is the effect of Positive economic effects on Support for universal healthcare immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think the effects are positive as more and more people get health care. There's going to be more money funded into the health care system and this is going to transfer to other areas within the local and national economic system.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Is the effect of Balancing healthcare policy burdens on Support for universal healthcare immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think it needs to be immediate. There has to be a radical restructure of these, you know, not even burdens of support for universal health care. It just needs to be transferred from other areas of government that are not benefiting the people as a whole.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How confident are you that changes in Access to care lead to changes in Support for universal healthcare? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I'm very positive or confident that changes in access to health care will lead to changes in support for universal health care. As more people actually gain this access, they will have the experiences to share with their friends and family and other media sources, which will lead to more support.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How would you describe the relationship between Published results and Support for universal healthcare? Is it a strong or weak connection? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think that published results help people to see what's actually happening, so it will form a strong positive connection as more and more people see how the system actually works and that is a beneficial positive to the people.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: Is the effect of Positive effect on Support for universal healthcare immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I don't think it's immediate. It takes time to develop, and people would actually see how the system is going to work and the benefits that are going to be passed around to everybody. It takes time to get that experience.

session_1758601889923_2mbnhpp: How would you describe the relationship between Noticable change and Support for universal healthcare? Is it a strong or weak connection? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: Noticeable change is going to lead to an increasing effect for supporting it. If it's a bad change, it's going to lead to a bad decrease in support.
